raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8367.

The agent loop puts the trajectory score on the last response token. A multi-turn trajectory can end with a chat-template suffix that has `response_mask = 0`. The SWE agent recipe does this: its trajectories end with `['```', '<|im_end|>', '\n']`, mask `[1, 1, 0]`. GAE, REINFORCE++, ReMax, OTB and TIR-OTB ignore rewards on mask-0 tokens, so with these estimators the outcome score never reaches the model. GRPO and RLOO sum the rewards without the mask and are not affected.

This PR puts the score on the last `response_mask = 1` token. The scorer still sees the full trajectory. The estimators do not change.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+rm_scores
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

Not a duplicate: I checked the open PRs that change `agent_loop.py` and `core_algos.py`, and searched issues and PRs for the keywords. None changes where the score is placed. #8305 adds turn-level process rewards and keeps the outcome score on the last token. #7300 (merged) fixed REINFORCE++ propagation across observation tokens, which is a different problem.

### Test

Two CPU tests in `tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_agent_loop_extra_fields_schema_on_cpu.py`, one for each placement path:

- `test_agent_loop_output_as_dict_scores_last_generated_token`: `AgentLoopOutput.as_dict()`.
- `test_agent_loop_postprocess_scores_last_generated_token`: `AgentLoopWorker._postprocess()`, with a masked tail, a padded row, and a row with no generated token (the score stays on the last valid token).

```
pytest tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_agent_loop_extra_fields_schema_on_cpu.py
main:    2 failed, 19 passed
this PR: 21 passed
```

- All 6 `tests/experimental/agent_loop/*_on_cpu.py` files: 42 passed.
- Mutation check: each of the 3 edits (as_dict placement, `_postprocess` placement, the fallback for rows with no generated token) reverted one at a time. Each one makes a new test fail.
- End to end: a real SWE recipe trajectory (`TrajectoryReconstructor`, Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 tokenizer) through `as_dict()`, then GAE and REINFORCE++ with gamma = lam = 1 and V = 0. On main, the score is on token 50 of 51 (`\n`) and the return at the first token is 0.0 for both. With this PR, the score is on token 49 (`<|im_end|>`) and the return is 1.0.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: all hooks pass.

Not tested: a GPU training run.

### API and Usage Example

No API change.

### Design & Code Changes

`verl/experimental/agent_loop/agent_loop.py`:

- `AgentLoopOutput.as_dict()`: put the score on the last nonzero position of `response_mask`. If there is none, keep `[-1]`.
- `AgentLoopWorker._postprocess()`: the same rule for the padded batch. If a row has no generated token, keep the last valid token.

Not changed:

- Token-level rejection sampling can set the mask of the final generated token to 0 after the score is placed. It needs a separate decision (see #8367), so this PR does not change it.
- `RewardManagerBase.assemble_rm_scores` (colocated reward model) places the score the same way. On the v1 trainer its input has no `response_mask`, so I left it for a follow-up.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always`
- [ ] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs). Not needed: no API or config change.
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. If not feasible, explain why: the new tests are `*_on_cpu.py`, so `cpu_unit_tests.yml` runs them.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) in [the `verl` Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/verl-project/shared_invite/zt-3855yhg8g-CTkqXu~hKojPCmo7k_yXTQ). (If not accessible, please try [the Feishu group (飞书群)](https://applink.larkoffice.com/client/chat/chatter/add_by_link?link_token=772jd4f1-cd91-441e-a820-498c6614126a).)
- [ ] If your PR is related to the `recipe` submodule, please also update the reference to the submodule commit via `git submodule update --remote` or `cd recipe && git pull origin main`. Not related.

     assert merged.non_tensor_batch["tool_rewards"][0] == []
 
 
+def test_agent_loop_output_as_dict_scores_last_generated_token():
+    """as_dict puts the score on the last generated token, not on a trailing response_mask=0 token."""
+    output = AgentLoopOutput(
+        prompt_ids=[101, 102],

+        metrics=AgentLoopMetrics(),
+    )
+
+    fields = output.as_dict()
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(fields["rm_scores"], torch.tensor([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0]))
+
+
+def test_agent_loop_postprocess_scores_last_generated_token():
+    """_postprocess puts the score of each row on its last generated token, or on its last valid token."""
+    rows = [
+        # (response_ids, response_mask, expected score index)
+        ([11, 12, 13], [1, 1, 0], 1),  # trailing chat-template suffix
+        ([11, 12], [1, 1], 1),  # ends with a generated token, padded to width 4
+        ([11, 12, 13], [0, 0, 0], 2),  # no generated token: keep the last valid token
+    ]
+    inputs = []
+    for i, (response_ids, response_mask, _) in enumerate(rows):
+        internal = _to_internal(
+            output_prompt_ids=[101, 102],
+            output_response_ids=response_ids,
+            output_response_mask=response_mask,
+            metrics=AgentLoopMetrics(),
+            extra_fields={},
+            num_turns=2,
+            prompt_len=2,
+            response_len=4,
+        )
+        internal.reward_score = float(i + 1)
+        inputs.append(internal)
+    dummy_worker = type(
+        "_DummyWorker",
+        (),
+        {"reward_loop_worker_handles": None, "distillation_enabled": False},
+    )()
+
+    merged = AgentLoopWorker._postprocess(dummy_worker, inputs=inputs)
+
+    expected = torch.zeros(len(rows), 4)
+    for i, (_, _, index) in enumerate(rows):
+        expected[i, index] = float(i + 1)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(merged.batch["rm_scores"], expected)
+
+
